messages.author: 34f79c4acd5c30e7
messages.subject: geom_density Bandwidth
parts:
Is there any way to specify the kernel bandwidth geom_density or stat_density?

It seems like this would be an obvious option but all I found is an
"adjust" parameter to scale the default bandwidth.

I have faceted data which I want to be plotted with the same
bandwidth, but the bandwidth estimation algorithm returns very
different bandwidths for each facet.

Is there no way to specify the bandwidth directly?

-Scott

messages.author: 065110cca96a6373
messages.subject: Re: geom_density Bandwidth
parts:
Hi Scott,

It looks like the actual calculations for stat_density() are done
using MASS::kde2d which makes me wonder if just using h would work?
Can you provide an example of what is happening? I am not sure how
you are finding the bandwidth that was actually used. For instance,
in this data I tried to create, things *seem* comparable to me (maybe
I grossly misunderstand density, or maybe it is lousy data to
illustrate what you are talking about, but without an example, it is
hard to know):

dat <- data.frame(A = sample(1:10, 300, replace = TRUE),
G = factor(rep(1:3, each = 100)))

ggplot(data = dat, aes(x = A)) +
stat_density() + facet_grid(. ~ G)


Best regards,

Josh
